title: Did bands use the Red Book; Petit's tone and ability
summary: Hall says Petit read well, was the best trumpeter in his estimation, played mellow within the staff and seemed well schooled.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did they use the Red Book much down here when you were here?
No, because practically all these tunes that everybody knew them, you know, so many bands play them, you know. They said we didn't use them. Did Buddy read pretty well? Yeah, Buddy was a musician.
Yeah. You think he's one of the greatest, or maybe the greatest one that would make you pick on the spot.
Yeah, but in my estimation, he is, he is the, he was the guy for trumpet.
Did he play any other instrument to get his ear developed?
Not that I know of. Not that I know of.
I was wondering, because he seemed to know the chords and everything, I thought that he studied it.

No, I don't know what his father, I don't know what his father, was his people any musician or not, but I don't know where he got it from, but he was a good musician. I don't know where he got it from, where he picked it up.
Well, we don't want to keep you, I know you have other things to do. Oh, I have time. I just don't think of it. Hey Dad, this is a pleasure.
Anything else about Buddy Petit that we can think of? Did he play high or low? No, no, no, no.
He wasn't, he didn't play too high. He was always right there in the staff, you know, and he really, he's a really good player.

If we never heard him, we would have somebody, we would have to ask all these foolish questions, but since we didn't, we wonder sometimes how he did sound. Did he play somewhat like Louis' style, you think? Well, except Louis, of course, plays high now. Yeah. But I mean, do you think, it was a nice mellow tone?

Yeah, he had a nice tone. Well, to be frank with the way he played, he seemed, you could tell that he was, he was well schooled. You know what he was doing. He knew his instrument. There's no question about that. That's the thing that, yeah, kind of got me arrested, you know?
